paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God cares about the whole bakery, not just the Sunday part. In one breath He talks about altars and in the next He talks about oxen, loans and courtrooms. For Him, how you worship and how you treat your neighbor are one batch of dough. He starts with Himself, telling them not to make gods of silver or gold, and then He works His way down into everyday life (Exodus 20:23).

And look at who He keeps watching out for. The foreigner, the widow, the orphan, the poor man who needs his cloak to sleep in. God says, "You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt" (Exodus 22:21). Of the poor man's cry He says, "I will hear, for I am compassionate" (Exodus 22:27). I know a little about being forgotten in the dark, friend, and I can tell you it matters that God hears.

So here's what I'd carry out of this one. Being God's people shows up in small things: honest words in court, a donkey you help when you'd rather not, and the best of what you have brought to Him (Exodus 23:1, 5, 19). He says, "You are to be My holy people" (Exodus 22:31). That is not a cold list of rules to get through. It's God showing His people what it looks like to belong to Him, and this teaching isn't done yet.
